entries.title: Cluster overview
entries.summary: Top-level health and capacity snapshot for the whole cluster.
entries.description: The Cluster overview is the landing page. It aggregates validation progress, node and rack counts, GPU capacity, and live scheduler activity into stat tiles plus a cluster-wide active-job summary, so you can judge the state of the deployment at a glance before drilling into a rack.
features: Stat tiles for total racks, nodes, GPUs, and validation progress (done / failed / ongoing / pending).
Cluster metadata (project name, site, platform) with an inline editor.
Cluster-wide active-job overview summarising running and pending work.
Refresh control to re-pull live status from the head node.

steps: Open Compute > Cluster overview.
Read the validation stat tiles (done, failed, ongoing, pending).
Click a count to jump to the Racks list filtered by that state.
Find the cluster metadata card on the overview.
Click edit, update the project name / site fields, and save.
The overview refreshes to reflect the new metadata.

faqs.q: Why are some counts zero in demo mode?
faqs.a: When RACK_STATUS_DEMO=1 the app returns synthetic data; counts reflect the mock cluster, not a real head node.

tips: Use the Refresh button in the toolbar to re-pull cluster status without reloading the page.

aria.label: Cluster overview page
aria.description: Top-level cluster dashboard showing validation progress, rack and node counts, GPU capacity, and live scheduler activity.

entries.aiContext: The Cluster overview is the landing dashboard. It shows aggregate validation progress (done/failed/ongoing/pending), rack/node/GPU counts, cluster metadata, and a cluster-wide active-job summary. Users come here for a high-level health snapshot before drilling into individual racks.

entries.title: Racks
entries.summary: Sortable, filterable table of every rack and its validation status.
entries.description: The Racks page is the main working table. Each row is a rack showing its validation state, latest job, comment, and quick actions. You can sort and filter, click the status summary tags to filter by state, add comments, open parser charts, and click a rack to open its detail view.
features: Sortable/filterable table of all racks with validation state and metadata.
Clickable status summary tags (done/fail/ongoing/pending) that filter rows.
Per-rack row menu: open detail, view parser charts, tail logs, run actions.
Command activity indicator showing in-flight jobs per rack.

steps: Open Compute > Racks.
Click the rack name (or its row) to open the rack detail view.
Click one of the status summary tags above the table (e.g. Failed).
The table filters to racks in that state.
Click the tag again to clear the filter.

howTo.task: Add or edit a rack comment
steps: Find the rack's comment cell.
Click to edit, type your note, and confirm to save.

aria.label: Racks validation table
aria.description: Sortable, filterable table of all racks showing validation status, latest job, comments, and per-rack actions.

entries.aiContext: The Racks page is the main table listing every rack with its validation state, latest job, and comment. Users sort/filter, click status summary tags to filter by state, edit comments, open parser charts, and click a rack to open its detail view (rackDetail).

entries.title: Nodes
entries.summary: Flat, filterable inventory of every compute node with per-node actions.
entries.description: The Nodes page lists every compute node across the cluster in one paginated table (18 rows by default, one NVL72 rack in view). Filter by datacenter row, rack, or node name, then select a single node to run Validation, Hardware, Networking, and Services actions scoped to just that node. Node inventory and up/down state come from the same live status feed the Racks and Rack Detail views use.
features: Paginated node table (default 18 rows) with sortable node names.
Filters for row, rack, and node name.
Per-node status tag (UP / DOWN / INST / UNKNOWN) and BMC/RedFish link.
Select a node to expose Validation, Hardware, Networking, and Services action tabs scoped to that node.
Bring-up results panel: per-job status, metric, and reason from the cluster automation (results + reports), with open-log and NCCL charts per job.

howTo.task: Run an action on a single node
steps: Open Compute > Nodes.
Filter by rack or name to find the node.
Click the node row to select it.
Open the relevant action tab (Validation, Hardware, Networking, Services) and confirm.

howTo.task: Narrow the list to one rack
steps: Use the Rack filter and pick one or more racks.
The table and pagination update to the matching nodes.

tips: The default page size is 18 so a single NVL72 rack fits on one page.
Actions here apply to the one selected node; use the Racks view to act on a whole rack.

aria.label: Nodes inventory page

entries.aiContext: The Nodes page is a flat, paginated inventory of every compute node (default 18 rows). Users filter by row, rack, or name and select a single node to run Validation, Hardware, Networking, and Services actions scoped to that node. A Bring-up results panel shows per-job status/metric/reason from the cluster automation (Travis's /home/cmods/bringup results + reports, via /api/bringup/node) with open-log and NCCL charts per job. Node/tray state reuses the same live status feed as the Racks and Rack Detail views.

entries.title: Multirack operations
entries.summary: Run validation and commands across many racks at once.
entries.description: Multirack operations lets you select several racks and launch the same validation or command across all of them, then monitor aggregated progress and tail combined logs. It is built for campaign-style validation where you energise and verify many racks in sequence.
features: Select multiple racks and launch a shared validation/command.
Aggregated progress tracking across the selected racks.
Combined log tailing for the multirack run.
Parser results across the selected set.

howTo.task: Run a validation across multiple racks
steps: Open Compute > Multirack operations.
Select the racks to include.
Choose the validation/command and start the run.
Watch aggregated progress and tail logs as it executes.

tips: Validate one rack at a time when possible; require all nodes healthy before starting a multirack campaign.

entries.title: Rack detail
entries.summary: Drill-down for one rack: status, nodes, and validation/hardware actions.
entries.description: The Rack detail view is where you operate on a single rack. It opens with an overview card (validation tag, node availability, last job, comment), a node selector to scope actions to specific nodes, and tabs that group the available commands: Validation, Hardware, Networking, and Services. Most actions run via an ActionCard with a confirmation and stream live output.
features: Overview card: validation state, node availability, last job, comment, key fields.
Node selector: multi-select nodes/trays, per-node terminal, issue-count trend and full in-SPA history.
Validation tab: NEMO, burn-in, NCCL/parser runs for selected nodes.
Hardware tab: repeatable deep audit with automatic scheduler comment/drain, plus hardware checks, power reset and MAC change.
Networking tab: repeatable forced-NVLink/IB deep audit with automatic scheduler comment/drain; Services holds service commands.
Live streaming output, last-output indicator, and rack lock awareness.

howTo.task: Run a validation on specific nodes
steps: Open a rack from the Racks table.
In the node selector, select the target nodes.
Switch to the Validation tab and pick the action card (e.g. NEMO).
Confirm in the dialog; watch the streamed output.

howTo.task: Power-cycle / reset hardware on a node
steps: Select the node(s) in the node selector.
Open the Hardware tab.
Use the power reset / hardware action card and confirm.

howTo.task: Open a web terminal to a node
steps: Select the node.
Use the per-node terminal action to open a web terminal session.

howTo.task: Run a deep audit and review node history
steps: Select the target nodes and open Hardware or Networking.
Click Start Tests on the deep-audit card; confirmed failures are commented and drained through the active scheduler.
Click Results beside Start Tests for the per-node audit result and corrective action.
Click ▲n in the node selector to see validation participation, evidence-attributed failures, and detailed Rack Status findings.

faqs.q: Why am I warned that the rack is locked?
faqs.a: Another operator holds an advisory lock on the rack. Coordinate before running commands; the lock conflict dialog shows who holds it.

tips: Scope actions to selected nodes to avoid acting on the whole rack unintentionally.

aria.label: Rack detail page
aria.description: Per-rack workspace with an overview card, a node selector, and Validation, Hardware, Networking, and Services action tabs.

entries.aiContext: The Rack detail view operates on one rack. Its node selector adds a validation-history ▲ issue trend; clicking it opens evidence-attributed run and finding history without leaving the SPA. Hardware Deep Audit and NVLink / Network Deep Audit are repeatable durable workflows with Results next to Start Tests. Only structured, confirmed node failures are automatically recorded, given a specific scheduler reason containing the workflow id, and drained; warnings/skips/transport failures remain inconclusive.

entries.title: Hardware tab
entries.summary: Deep hardware audit with automatic scheduler drain, plus hardware actions.
entries.description: The Hardware tab starts with a repeatable GB300 deep audit of GPU inventory/thermal/ECC/recovery, Xid/PCIe/EDAC, services, IMEX and storage. Results is beside Start Tests. A structured confirmed failure is recorded and immediately commented/drained through the active scheduler; warnings and unavailable probes do not drain. Power, MAC, hw-check and other cards remain below it.
features: Hardware deep audit with per-node durable results.
Automatic specific scheduler comment and drain for confirmed failures.

entries.title: Networking tab
entries.summary: Forced-NVLink/IB deep audit with automatic scheduler drain, plus network actions.
entries.description: The Networking tab starts with a repeatable GB300 deep audit covering NVLink fabric and a forced data-path probe, IMEX, IB rails/rates/error counters and mlx5 bonding. Results is beside Start Tests. Confirmed node failures are recorded and immediately commented/drained through the active scheduler; skipped probes remain explicit and do not count as a pass or trigger a drain.

entries.title: Terminal
entries.summary: A grid of live head-node and compute shells, side by side in one workspace.
entries.description: The Terminal page is a workspace of live shells. Add terminal opens a searchable picker of every compute node in the active cluster plus the head node; each one you add becomes a pane in a grid that grows from one full-width shell to two side by side, then two by two, and on from there. Panes are dragged by their header (the terminal body stays selectable) and resized from their corner, and the shell reflows to whatever size you give it. A single pane detaches to its own browser tab, or Detach grid moves the whole arrangement to a new tab at once. Detaching hands over the running session rather than dialling a second one, so it is a move, not a duplicate. Your panes and their arrangement are remembered per cluster; the sessions themselves end with the page.
features: Searchable picker over every compute node in the active cluster, plus the head node.
Grid grows 1x1 to 2x1 to 2x2 as you add shells; drag by the header, resize from the corner.

entries.aiContext: Tools > Terminal is a react-grid-layout workspace of live xterm.js shells over the dashboard's SSH path. Add terminal opens a picker listing compute nodes (derived from rack rows by parseNodesFromRack) plus the head node (target 'headnode', mode 'headnode'). Panes auto-place 1x1 -> 2x1 -> 2x2 and are draggable by header only so terminal text stays selectable. A pane detaches to /terminal?session=<id> and the whole grid to /terminal-grid?g=<base64url>, both carrying live session ids so shells are adopted rather than reopened. Layout persists per cluster in localStorage; sessions do not survive a reload.

entries.title: Analytics
entries.summary: Rack-level and node-level analytics, plus the cluster and customer-schema reports.
entries.description: The Analytics page has two tabs. Rack Level aggregates rack and benchmark data into cluster-wide charts and tables — validation pass rates, NCCL/NEMO benchmark trends, and comparisons across racks. Node Level shows a heatmap with one square per node, coloured by a selectable data view (node up/down, test completion, or any bring-up benchmark that produces a metric such as NCCL busbw), with each node's up/down state always drawn as the square's border. The Compact layout tiles racks eight across as blocks of trays so a whole floor fits on one screen; Linear gives each rack its own row and shows a load gauge per node. The heatmap can be downloaded as a PNG or JPEG image. The Rack Level tab carries a report generator offering two reports: the Rack Status standard report (cluster details plus a row per node, as CSV, JSON, or a PDF with rack-level charts) and the Nscale TX JSON schema report (the customer's Consolidated Test Plan contract, schema-validated before download).
features: Rack Level: cluster-wide aggregate charts, benchmark trends, cross-rack comparisons.
Node Level: per-node heatmap grouped by rack, with a data-view selector.
Compact layout tiles racks as blocks with a per-rack tally; Linear shows a gauge per node.
Test completion view: all tests done, partial, or none run — independent of pass/fail.
Up/down state shown as each cell's border on every view.
Metric views scale against the fleet's observed range, stated in the legend.
Download image: the heatmap as a report-ready PNG or JPEG with title, legend and timestamp.

Report generator (Rack Level tab): the Rack Status report as CSV/JSON/PDF, or the Nscale TX schema report as validated JSON. Both sweep every node for hardware and firmware identity, with a progress bar.

aria.label: Analytics page
aria.description: Rack-level and node-level analytics with downloadable cluster reports.

entries.aiContext: The Analytics page has a Rack Level tab (cluster-wide aggregate charts: validation pass rates, NCCL/NEMO trends, cross-rack comparisons) and a Node Level tab (per-node heatmap grouped by rack; the fill is a selectable view — node up/down, test completion, or a bring-up metric like NCCL busbw — and the border always shows up/down). Test completion counts a test as done once it has a verdict, pass or fail, so it answers 'has this node been tested' rather than 'did it pass'. Two layouts: Compact tiles racks eight across as tray blocks with a per-rack good/warn/bad tally (the whole floor on one screen), Linear gives each rack a row and each node a load gauge. Metric views auto-scale to the fleet's observed range. Download image renders the heatmap to a light-background PNG/JPEG with title, legend, cluster and timestamp baked in, drawn on a canvas so it does not depend on the UI theme. The Rack Level tab carries a report generator with two reports. The Rack Status standard report renders one dataset as CSV, JSON, or a PDF with an executive summary and rack-level charts. The Nscale TX JSON schema report answers the customer's Consolidated Test Plan contract and is validated against the vendored schema before download, so it is JSON only; fields bring-up cannot measure are marked TBD for the operator to edit. Both reports share one fleet sweep of per-node hardware and firmware identity — asking twice while a sweep runs joins the running job rather than starting a second one — and report progress per node. PDF is only offered when the image can render it.

entries.title: Validation Status
entries.summary: Floor-style node validation participation, failure trends, deep audits, and scheduler status.
entries.description: Validation Status combines live bring-up checks, current Slurm state, durable validation activities, exact scheduler targets, and deep-audit findings. The default All view spans every discovered validation domain, while selectors isolate Node Health, DCGM, NCCL, NeMo, Llama, MNUberGEMM, and source-specific jobs. Selecting a node shows Job IDs, checks, metrics, failure reasons, evidence timestamps, and the complete validation history.
features: Punchcard-style floor view grouped by rack, with run and attributed-failure counts per node.
Increasing, decreasing, flat, and new failure trends; a repeat flag requires at least three findings across three distinct runs.
Node drill-down with every validation participation, Job ID, scheduler state, evidence category, and finding.
Current scheduler state and reason shown beside validation history.
Persistent Node hardware status and Node network status report sections.
One-node hardware or NVLink/network deep audits can be launched from the investigation dialog.
Operator findings can be recorded locally or explicitly attached to a scheduler drain after confirmation.

steps: Open Analytics & Benchmarks > Validation Status.
Select All or a validation domain.
Hover a node for current evidence, then select it.
Review checks, Job IDs, metrics, failure reasons, and current scheduler comment.
Launch the relevant hardware or NVLink/network audit and watch the 30-second live view refresh.

howTo.task: Record and drain a confirmed node issue
steps: Open the node from the floor view.
Choose an evidence category and enter the exact reason.
Enable the scheduler drain option.
Confirm the exact node; Rack Status records the finding and applies the generated scheduler reason.

tips: A failed multi-node job is visible as participation but does not count against every tray. A node failure requires explicit evidence, a single-node job, or a structured audit/operator finding.

aria.label: Validation Status page
aria.description: Live SU, rack, and node validation map with domain filters, job evidence, predictions, and downloadable reports.

entries.aiContext: This page is the first-class post-run node history, not a Google punchcard import. It joins durable validation activities to exact scheduler targets, snapshots node membership, counts attributed failures only with node-specific evidence, flags repeat offenders across distinct runs, and shows current scheduler state/reason. It has persistent hardware and NVLink/network report sections. A selected node can launch either deep audit or receive an operator mark; draining requires an explicit confirmation.

entries.title: Reports
entries.summary: Download saved cluster reports, plus bug report and NVLMapper archives.
entries.description: The Reports page holds two separate things. Generated reports are the cluster and customer-schema documents produced from Analytics > Rack Level; each is saved when it finishes, so you can start a report, leave the page, and download it here later — a fleet sweep takes minutes and is no longer lost by navigating away. Rows show the report type, format, when it was generated, the node count it covers, and any schema errors, and can be downloaded or deleted. Below that, the bug report section lists NVIDIA bug report archives, NVLMapper outputs and Excel exports already present in the reports directory on this dashboard host.
features: Generated Rack Status (CSV/JSON/PDF) and Nscale TX schema (JSON) reports, saved automatically when they finish.
Reports survive leaving the page and a container restart; the most recent are kept and older ones pruned.
Schema errors are shown on the row, so a report that failed validation is visible without regenerating it.
Separate listing of nvidia-bug-report archives, NVLMapper CSV/XLS and parser Excel exports from the reports directory.

howTo.task: Get a report you generated earlier

You can leave the page; it appears here when the sweep finishes.

aria.label: Reports page
aria.description: Download saved cluster reports and node bug report archives.

entries.aiContext: Analytics > Reports lists (1) generated reports from report_store.py, served by GET /api/reports/generated with download and DELETE at /api/reports/generated/<id>, kept under var/reports on the rack-data volume so they survive restarts, and (2) bug report / NVLMapper files from the reports directory via /api/bug-report-inventory. Reports are archived by the node-report worker when it completes, not when downloaded, so closing the tab mid-sweep no longer loses the run. Generation itself happens on Analytics > Analytics, Rack Level tab.

entries.title: API Reference
entries.summary: Browsable reference for this deployment's REST API, generated from its own routes.
entries.description: API Reference renders the OpenAPI 3.1 document served at /api/openapi.json, which the backend generates from its own Flask route table on each request. Because it is generated rather than maintained, it cannot describe an endpoint this build does not serve, and a new endpoint appears without anyone editing a file. Operations are grouped by endpoint family, searchable by path, verb, group or summary, and each one shows its parameters, request body and the status codes its handler actually returns.
features: Every /api/* operation with its verb, path, summary and full description from the handler's docstring.
Query parameters are the ones each handler actually reads, so the page cannot claim a parameter the code ignores.
Download the raw document as JSON (or /api/openapi.yaml) to generate a client or import into other tooling.

steps: Open API Reference.
Type a path, verb or keyword in the filter.
Click an operation to expand its parameters and responses.
Open API Reference.
Click 'openapi.json' to download the document.
Point your client generator at it; authenticate first via POST /api/login.

aria.label: API reference page

entries.aiContext: API Reference renders /api/openapi.json, an OpenAPI 3.1 document generated from the Flask route table (about 177 paths / 201 operations). Query parameters are derived from what each handler reads; request bodies are free-form JSON by design rather than schema'd. The raw document is available at /api/openapi.json and /api/openapi.yaml, behind the normal auth gate.
